classification.difficultyReason: Connects the familiar cone volume formula with an explicitly supplied definite integral.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Consider the region bounded by the line $y=3x$ and the $x$-axis between $x=0$ and $x=3$.

spec.description: Unshaded straight-line graph with both-ended axes and line arrows; no boundary at x=3.
spec.mathematics: y=3x; horizontal labels -1,1,2,3,4; vertical labels every 2 from -10 to 10 excluding zero.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph is visible in every edition.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
When this region is rotated about the $x$-axis, a right circular cone is formed.

Find the radius and height of the cone and hence find its volume using $V=\frac13\pi r^2h$.

answer.worked:
At $x=3$, $y=3(3)=9$, so $r=9$ units and $h=3$ units.
$$\begin{align*}V&=\frac13\pi r^2h\\V&=\frac13\pi(9^2)(3)\\V&=81\pi\text{ units}^3\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\pi\int_0^3 9x^2\,dx&=\pi\left[3x^3\right]_0^3\\&=\pi\left(3(3)^3-3(0)^3\right)\\&=81\pi\text{ units}^3\end{align*}$$
This agrees with the cone formula.
